General information.Name: Environmental impact of Oaxaca cheese production and wastewater from artisanal dairies under two scenarios in Aculco, State of Mexico
General information.Description: The environmental impacts in the artisan cheese sector in the central region of Mexico provide a particular panorama of the environmental situation of this industry. The objective of this study was to evaluate environmental impacts through a life cycle analysis in 10 impact categories: global warming, stratospheric ozone depletion, fine particle formation, ozone formation, terrestrial ecosystems, terrestrial acidification, eutrophication of fresh water, terrestrial ecotoxicity, human ecotoxicity. non-carcinogenic toxicity, scarcity of fossil resources and water consumption. And the calculation of the carbon footprint with the IPCC, 2013 of 1 kg of Oaxaca cheese in four dairies artisanal in the State of Mexico. The main hotspots were whey, transportation, and electricity. The reduction of the impact generated by wastewater can be associated with the implementation and improvement of eco-innovations such as the use of biodigesters, however their use generates impacts on SOD, TA, FA, TEc and FRs due to the composition of the whey residue. The renewal of refrigeration equipment is another alternative to reduce electricity consumption, which on average consumes 0.04 kWh per one kg of Oaxaca cheese in cheese factories that have new refrigerators, and 0.14 kWh when refrigerators are reused, mainly impacting the FRs. The average carbon footprint of Oaxaca cheese was 15.6 CO2 kg eq, which allows us to have a measure of the behavior of this food. A sensitivity analysis was carried out with different scenarios with wastewater where it was found that the handling of whey is essential for reducing impacts.
General information.Tags: Artisanal cheese, WWT anaerobic, carbon footprint, Whey, Eco-innovations, Life Cycle Assessment, Environmental impact
General information.Technology | Description: The life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology is used to know environmental impacts in a product or service. Is a tool that is internationally recognized for the quality of its data and procedures. Specialized software is available for carrying out LCAs (SIMAPRO, OpenLCA, Umberto) that relies on extensive environmental databases, enabling complete environmental inventories (calculation of all inputs and outputs to a system and used as a method within the LCAs) to be completed using global data. The software SimaPro® v.8.5.0.0 (PRé Sustainability, Amersfoort, Netherlands) was used to calculate the environmental impacts. Inputs such as raw milk, detergent ingredients to clean and desinfect (biodegradable soap to clean), and wastewater input were obtained from the Ecoinvent v.3 database (Ecoinvent, Zurich, Switzerland). The impact evaluation was made using the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint impacts categories method, Herarquista (H) v 1.01, SimaPro® v.8.5.0.0 (PhD version).

processDocumentation.LCI method: Life cycle assessment (LCA) according to ISO 14040 using SimaPro® v.8.5.0.0 software with ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint impacts categories method, Herarquista (H) v 1.01
processDocumentation.Process type: Artisanal cheese production system from raw milk reception to product delivery at retail market (cradle-to-gate)
processDocumentation.Modeling constants: Functional unit: 1 kg of Oaxaca cheese; 10% of whey considered as lost and allocated to wastewater; 90% of whey considered as avoided product for pig feeding; Time horizon of 100 years for carbon footprint calculation according to IPCC 2013
processDocumentation.Data source information: Primary data collected through direct observation and 18 semi-structured interviews with cheese-making personnel and dairy owners over one-year period (June 2018 to June 2019); Secondary data from Ecoinvent v.3 database and Mexican electrical energy database; Physicochemical analysis of cheese samples conducted in triplicate
processDocumentation.Data completeness: Complete coverage of all relevant flows within system boundaries including raw materials, energy, water, transportation, and waste outputs; Milk production stage excluded from system boundaries
processDocumentation.Data selection: Included all inputs and outputs directly related to Oaxaca cheese production; Excluded milk production stage to focus on cheese industry critical points; Included transportation for both input acquisition and product distribution
processDocumentation.Data treatment: Monthly production data calculated first, then annual averages estimated for functional unit; Data verified using multifunction energy meter WR D-024; Statistical analysis using Shapiro-Wilk test and one-way ANOVA for physicochemical data
processDocumentation.Sampling procedure: Snowball method for participant identification; Four dairies selected for LCA; Cheese samples obtained from each dairy in April 2019; All measurements made in triplicate
processDocumentation.Data collection period: One-year period from June 2018 to June 2019
processDocumentation.Use advice: Results specific to artisanal Oaxaca cheese production in Aculco, State of Mexico; Not applicable to industrial cheese production or other geographical regions; Assumes 90% whey reuse as pig feed
processDocumentation.Completeness: Comprehensive coverage of all production stages from milk reception to retail delivery; Complete inventory of inputs and outputs; 10 impact categories evaluated
processDocumentation.Sources: Aguirre-Villegas et al., 2011; Canellada et al., 2018; Berlin, 2002; Finnegan et al., 2017; Ecoinvent v.3 database; Santoyo-Castelazo et al., 2011
processDocumentation.Project: CONACYT project 'Estudio de productos lácteos en el norte del estado de México a través de un S-ACV: Estudio de caso de dos tipos de quesos' 4285/2017/CI and PAPIIT-IN305620 'Repertorios y estrategias culturales de organizaciones y actores en la sustentabilidad de la cadena agroalimentaria de productos lácteos'
processDocumentation.Intended application: Environmental impact assessment of artisanal cheese dairies; Identification of hotspots for improvement; Carbon footprint calculation; Comparison of wastewater management scenarios
processDocumentation.Data set owner: Universidad Autónoma del Estado de México and Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México
processDocumentation.Data set generator: Cristina Salas-Vargas, Luis Brunett-Pérez, Valentín Efrén Espinosa-Ortiz, Carlos Galdino Martínez-García
processDocumentation.Data set documentor: Cristina Salas-Vargas, Luis Brunett-Pérez, Valentín Efrén Espinosa-Ortiz, Carlos Galdino Martínez-García
processDocumentation.Access and use restrictions: Copyright restrictions apply; Available through ScienceDirect with appropriate subscriptions
